name: prefers-tables
description: User wants comparisons rendered as markdown tables rather than prose
content: When comparing two or more options, render the comparison as a markdown table. Prose comparisons get skimmed and the distinctions are lost.

name: terse-summaries
description: User wants short summaries at the end of a task, not a recap of every step
content: End a task with two or three sentences on what changed and what to watch. Do not re-narrate the steps; they were visible while they happened.

name: timezone-ist
description: User works in IST (UTC+5:30); schedule and deadline discussion assumes that zone
content: All dates and times discussed default to Asia/Kolkata unless stated otherwise.

name: background-rust
description: User is fluent in Rust and TypeScript, learning Go
content: Rust and TypeScript need no explanation of language basics. For Go, briefly explain idioms that differ from Rust, especially error handling and interfaces.

name: reviews-diffs-closely
description: User reads every line of a diff and dislikes unrelated formatting churn
content: Keep diffs surgical. Reformatting an untouched block, reordering imports, or fixing an unrelated typo all cost review time and hide the real change.

name: no-speculative-abstraction
description: Do not add configurability or interfaces that were not asked for
content:
**Why:** every unused extension point is code that must be read, tested, and kept working.
**How to apply:** write the single-use version. Extract an abstraction on the second caller, not the first.

name: ask-before-migrations
description: Always confirm before writing a database migration
content:
**Why:** migrations are hard to reverse once they run against a shared environment.
**How to apply:** show the SQL and the rollback path, then wait for an explicit go-ahead.

name: confirm-before-db-schema-change
description: Check with the user before altering database schema
content:
**Why:** a schema change against the shared dev database blocks everyone.
**How to apply:** describe the change and its rollback before applying it.

name: tests-before-fix
description: Write a failing test that reproduces a bug before fixing it
content:
**Why:** a fix without a reproduction cannot be shown to have fixed anything.
**How to apply:** reproduce, watch it fail, fix, watch it pass.

name: no-emoji-in-code
description: Never put emoji in source files, commit messages, or log output
content:
**Why:** they break terminal alignment and grep.
**How to apply:** plain ASCII in code and commits. Emoji are fine in chat.

name: explain-tradeoffs-first
description: State the tradeoff before recommending an approach
content:
**Why:** a recommendation without its cost cannot be evaluated.
**How to apply:** one sentence on what the approach gives up, then the recommendation.

name: commit-messages-imperative
description: Commit subject lines use the imperative mood and stay under 72 characters
content:
**Why:** matches the existing history and reads correctly in `git log --oneline`.
**How to apply:** "add retry to fetch", not "added" or "adding".

name: sse-stall-timeout
description: Settled on a 180s SSE stall timeout at the fetch layer rather than a total-duration cap
content: A silence timeout on live SSE streams, not a cap on total duration. A large tool call legitimately produces a long quiet stretch and a duration cap read it as a dead stream. The timeout lives at the fetch layer so it sees raw bytes; moving it above stream normalization drops tool-input deltas and reintroduces the bug.

name: header-timeout-300s
description: Response headers must arrive within 300 seconds or the request is abandoned
content: Separate from the stall timeout: this one covers a provider that accepts a connection and never responds at all.

name: sqlite-over-postgres
description: Chose SQLite for the thread store because deployments are single-machine
content: No deployment runs more than one backend process, so the operational cost of Postgres buys nothing. Revisit if a hosted multi-tenant mode ships.

name: thread-store-sqlite
description: The thread store is backed by SQLite, not Postgres
content: Single-machine deployments only. A JSON store exists as a fallback for environments without the native module.

name: frontends-are-dumb
description: All business logic lives in the backend; frontends only render and speak IPC
content: TUI, VS Code, and web are presentation layers. No provider calls, no file reading, no tool execution in a frontend. The rule exists because logic duplicated across four frontends drifts within a release.

name: no-browser-automation
description: The Playwright browser path is legacy and must not be extended
content: API providers are the default execution path. The browser controller stays for compatibility but takes no new features.

name: release-binary-is-bun
description: The only distributable binary is the bun build; the SEA build is a dev artifact
content: The bun build bundles the backend and sets a flag so it runs from anywhere. The SEA build ships only the terminal shell and spawns the backend from disk, so it works exclusively inside the monorepo. Copying a SEA build into the installed versions directory breaks the command everywhere except the repository root.

name: file-limit-150-lines
description: Files over roughly 150 lines should be decomposed
content: The agent loop is an explicit exception; it is a cohesive state machine and splitting it would scatter one flow across files.

name: prompt-cache-prefix-stability
description: The static system prefix must not change between turns or the prompt cache misses
content: Anything that varies per turn goes after the cached prefix with caching disabled. This is why the retrieved-memory block sits at the tail of the system array: moving it into the prefix would rewrite the cache on every save.

name: parallel-tool-batching
description: Read-only tool calls are executed in parallel batches; mutating calls run serially
content: Batching is decided by whether a tool declares itself read-only. A tool missing from the read-only list is treated as mutating, which is the safe default but silently serialises it.

name: auth-tokens-in-keychain
description: Provider API keys are stored in the OS keychain, never in the settings file
content: Settings files get committed by accident and shared in bug reports. The keychain is read at startup and the value never lands on disk in plaintext.

name: rate-limit-backoff-jitter
description: Retries on 429 use exponential backoff with full jitter
content: Without jitter, every concurrent request retries at the same instant and the second wave fails identically.

name: compaction-threshold-120k
description: History is compacted at 120k tokens rather than at the model's full window
content: Running near the window edge made every turn expensive for no quality gain. The threshold is configurable by environment variable.

name: hooks-fail-open
description: A hook that errors or times out never blocks the tool call it wraps
content: A broken hook must degrade the feature it implements, not the agent. The only exception is an explicit deny decision, which is the hook working correctly.

name: graph-sidecar-is-derived
description: The memory graph sidecar is derived state and can be deleted at any time
content: Markdown files are the only source of truth. Corruption, schema changes, and embedding-model changes are all resolved by deleting the sidecar and rebuilding it.

name: memory-injected-uncached
description: The retrieved-memory block is injected with caching disabled at the tail of the system array
content: It varies per turn by construction, so it cannot live in the cached prefix.

name: q3-launch-deadline
description: The desktop build must ship before the end of Q3
content: Signed installers for macOS and Windows are the blocking item; the Linux build already works.

name: no-mcp-server-mode
description: Serving our own tools over MCP is deliberately not built
content: An MCP client exists. Exposing tools as an MCP server is out of scope until someone asks for it.

name: lockfile-is-pnpm
description: The repository uses pnpm workspaces; npm and yarn lockfiles must not be committed
content: A stray package-lock.json makes CI resolve a different dependency tree than local development.

name: old-compaction-at-window-edge
description: Superseded: compaction used to trigger at the model's full context window
content: Replaced by the 120k threshold. Kept only as a record of why the change was made.

name: old-keys-in-settings-file
description: Superseded: API keys used to live in the settings JSON file
content: Replaced by keychain storage after a key was pasted into a public bug report.

name: provider-status-page
description: Provider incident status dashboard
content: Check this first when every request to one provider starts failing at once. It lags real incidents by a few minutes.

name: design-specs-directory
description: Architecture specifications live under the superpowers specs directory
content: The v4 architecture spec supersedes v3. Topical specs cover the agent loop, providers, memory, MCP, hooks, and observability.

name: onboarding-runbook
description: New-contributor setup runbook
content: Covers toolchain versions, the native module build, and how to run the backend against a local frontend.

name: perf-dashboard
description: Latency and token-cost dashboard for production sessions
content: Broken down by provider and model. Token cost is estimated, not billed, so it drifts from the invoice.

name: issue-tracker-project
description: The issue tracker board for this project
content: Bugs go in the triage column; anything with a customer impact gets the escalation label.

name: embedding-model-card
description: Model card for the local sentence-embedding model used by memory retrieval
content: 384 dimensions, runs locally, no API key. Documents the sequence-length limit that truncates long memories before embedding.

name: sqlite-wal-docs
description: Upstream documentation for SQLite write-ahead logging
content: Explains the checkpoint behaviour that made the store appear to leak disk space under heavy write load.
